title: Unit 3: LLM Decoding Parameters, Hallucinations & RAG Concepts

topics.title: Sampling & Decoding Parameters (Temperature, Top-p)
topics.starter_question: If an LLM hallucinates factual statements even when temperature is set to 0.0, why does zero temperature not prevent hallucination?

expectations.text: Temperature controls the flatness of the softmax token distribution, not the factual truth of pretraining knowledge.
Top-p dynamic nucleus sampling dynamically truncates the probability mass tail, maintaining coherent vocabulary selections.

misconceptions.label: Believing temperature = 0 eliminates hallucinations
misconceptions.description: Assuming greedy sampling guarantees factual correctness even when domain facts were never learned in training weights.

misconceptions.label: Confusing Top-k/Top-p token sampling with RAG top-k chunk retrieval
misconceptions.description: Conflating decoding hyperparameters with external document vector retrieval counts.

topics.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Grounding
topics.starter_question: When should you use Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) instead of prompt engineering or fine-tuning?

expectations.text: RAG injects dynamic, proprietary, or post-cutoff course excerpts directly into the prompt context window.
Grounding generation in retrieved chunks prevents extrinsic hallucinations and allows verifiable source citations.

misconceptions.label: Assuming LLMs query live databases natively
misconceptions.description: Believing foundation models possess real-time external knowledge without explicit retrieval augmentations or tools.
